summary: Iteration 21 — Security hardening + legal pages verified. Ran /app/backend/tests/test_security_iter21.py (9 tests, 6 pass, 3 fail — all 3 failures are infrastructure-layer effects, not backend code defects). Legal pages (/privacy-policy, /cookie-policy, /terms-of-use) render correctly with single H1, correct H2 counts (10/7/8), JSON-LD (BreadcrumbList+WebPage), canonical URLs with trailing slash, and proper CTA. Footer links (footer-privacy, footer-cookies, footer-terms) navigate correctly. Sitemap contains the 3 legal URLs with trailing slashes. POST /api/enquiries returns exactly {id, email_sent}. GET /api/enquiries returns 405 as expected. Security response headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security) all present on /api/health. HTML input sanitisation accepts

minor.issue: Backend correctly disables docs at FastAPI level (docs_url=None) and /api/docs returns 404. However the SPA catch-all route (path='*' → <Home />) makes root-level /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json return HTTP 200 with the React homepage instead of 404. Not a real information-disclosure risk (no Swagger UI is rendered) but violates the strict spec that these paths must 404. Fix option: add explicit backend routes returning 404, or update the ingress to reject these paths, or drop the SPA '*' route in favour of a proper NotFound page that returns 404 status.

Edge/Cloudflare layer intercepts and answers the OPTIONS preflight before reaching the backend, returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,PUT,DELETE,OPTIONS,HEAD,PATCH. This overrides the backend's locked CORS_ORIGINS list. From a strict browser-security stance this allows any origin to make CORS requests to /api. Backend CORSMiddleware config is correct; the fix is at the Kubernetes ingress / Cloudflare layer — either disable the edge CORS auto-response for this hostname, or align its allow-origin/allow-methods to match the backend's. Confirmed both apollobuilders.com.au and evil.example.com origins receive '*' back (evil is not echoed but wildcard is effectively permissive).

Rate limiter works per client-IP when a single source IP is observed (verified in backend logs: 'ratelimit 5 per 1 hour (10.208.151.75) exceeded'), and confirmed via serial curl (7 consecutive requests → 429). However `slowapi.util.get_remote_address` reads `request.client.host` (immediate TCP peer), not the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For. Behind the K8s ingress there are multiple nginx-proxy source IPs (observed both 10.208.151.74 and 10.208.151.75 in backend access logs during a single test session), which means a single real client can round-robin across multiple in-app rate-limit buckets, effectively doubling their allowance. Fix: define a custom key_func that reads X-Forwarded-For first (falling back to remote address), and configure Starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware / uvicorn --proxy-headers so `request.client.host` is trusted. Otherwise the '5/hour per IP' guarantee is weaker than intended in production.

action_items: Backend: swap slowapi key_func to read X-Forwarded-For so the 5/hour-per-IP rate limit is enforced against the real client IP behind the K8s/Cloudflare proxy (add uvicorn --proxy-headers or FastAPI ProxyHeadersMiddleware).
Infra: reconcile the Cloudflare/ingress-level CORS auto-response so it does NOT override the backend's locked CORS_ORIGINS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on OPTIONS preflights.
SPA: consider a real /404 route with HTTP 404 status so /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json don't 200 with the homepage. Cosmetic-security, not a real information leak.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: rate limiter uses `get_remote_address` — when the app is behind a reverse proxy this reads the proxy IP, not the client. This is a well-known slowapi footgun and directly weakens the 5/hour lockdown claimed in the review request. See action_items.

server.py: no request-body size cap on /api/enquiries beyond Pydantic field maxlengths. Consider `Content-Length` guard middleware for defence-in-depth against oversized bodies (Pydantic still allocates before validating).

rca of the issue: 1) /docs=200: React Router catch-all `<Route path='*' element={<Home />}>` in App.js serves the SPA for any non-API path, so /docs never reaches the backend (which correctly disables docs). 2) CORS wildcard: Kubernetes ingress + Cloudflare edge answers CORS preflight OPTIONS *before* the request reaches uvicorn, injecting Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * — verified by comparing edge response (ACAO:*, methods: GET,POST,PUT,DELETE,OPTIONS,HEAD,PATCH) against backend config (allow_methods=['GET','POST','OPTIONS'] only). 3) Rate limiter miss: `get_remote_address` returns `request.client.host` which is the nginx-proxy pod IP, not the true client. Backend logs show requests arriving from at least two different proxy source IPs (10.208.151.74 and 10.208.151.75) during a single test client's session, so an attacker or noisy user effectively gets N × 5/hour where N is the proxy pool size. Mitigation: `Limiter(key_func=lambda req: req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', get_remote_address(req)).split(',')[0].strip())` + `uvicorn --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'`.
